title: Un tinto antes del aguacero en Bogotá

dialogue.speaker: Natalia
dialogue.spanish: Uy, Andrés, mirá esas nubes negras sobre los cerros. Se va a venir un aguacero tenaz.
dialogue.english: Whoa, Andrés, look at those dark clouds over the hills. A fierce downpour is about to hit.

slang.actualMeaning: intense / fierce / crazy (very common Bogotá slang)
slang.example: El tráfico por la Séptima hoy está tenaz.

dialogue.speaker: Andrés
dialogue.spanish: Sí, qué frío tan berraco. Entremos a esta cafetería y nos tomamos un tinto bien caliente.
dialogue.english: Yeah, it's freezing cold. Let's duck into this café and have a piping hot black coffee.

slang.actualMeaning: a cup of black coffee (in Colombia, 'tinto' means black coffee, not red wine!)
slang.example: ¿Me regala un tinto sin azúcar, por favor?

dialogue.speaker: Natalia
dialogue.spanish: Buena idea. Y pidamos dos almojábanas recién salidas del horno mientras escampa.
dialogue.english: Good idea. And let's order two cheese breads fresh out of the oven while the rain lets up.

dialogue.speaker: Andrés
dialogue.spanish: Listo, de una. Apenas pare la lluvia caminamos a la estación de TransMilenio.
dialogue.english: Done, let's do it. As soon as the rain stops we'll walk to the TransMilenio bus station.

slang.actualMeaning: right away / let's do it / count me in

questions.question: Why do Natalia and Andrés decide to duck into a café in Bogotá?
options: It's freezing cold and a heavy rainstorm ('aguacero') is about to start
They have a business meeting with a client there
Andrés needs Wi-Fi to send an email
questions.explanation: Natalia sees dark clouds ('se va a venir un aguacero tenaz') and Andrés says it's freezing cold ('qué frío tan berraco').

questions.question: What food do they order to go with their hot drinks?
options: Two warm cheese breads ('almojábanas') fresh from the oven
questions.explanation: Natalia says: 'Y pidamos dos almojábanas recién salidas del horno mientras escampa.'

questions.question: What is their plan once the rain stops ('mientras escampa')?
options: Walk to the TransMilenio bus station
Call a taxi to go to the airport
questions.explanation: Andrés says: 'Apenas pare la lluvia caminamos a la estación de TransMilenio.'

questions.question: Slang Side Quest: When Andrés orders 'un tinto bien caliente' in Colombia, what is he ordering?
options: A cup of hot black coffee (not red wine!)
A glass of mulled red wine
A cup of hot chocolate with cheese
questions.explanation: False-friend alert! In Colombia, 'un tinto' always means a small cup of black coffee, whereas in Spain 'vino tinto' is red wine.
